To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Rho-kinases mediate LIMK- 1 activation, which leads to cofilin phosphorylation, but in LPA-stimu- lated platelets, cofilin is dephosphory- lated by an unknown mechanism.
LIMK-activity in platelets is not required for LPA-stimulating shape change, and that the dephosphorylaton of cofilin is independent of LIMK and is Ca(2+) dependent.
LPA-stimulatet platelets induce a Ca2+-dependent rapid dephospho-rylation of cofiline which precedes the increase of F actin and secretion and aggregation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cofilin in platelet shape change and aggregation.
a novel role of cofilin in platelet secretion and aggregation.
the role of cofilin in LPA-induced platelet activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LPA-induced cofilin activation is a complex and multi-faceted process, which is dependent on the stimulus and the presence or absence of fibrin(ogen).
in platelets, ROK-dependent LIMK activation leads to cofilin phosphorylation, but this phosphorylation is rapidly reversed by cofilin de-phosphorylation.

cofilin deactivation in LPA-activated platelets is mediated by a Rho- and Ca(2+)/calmodulin-dependent pathway, and that cofilin is not involved in the F-actine increase during platelet shape change, whereas it is involved in the regulation of secretion and aggregation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cofilin phosphorylation/dephosphorylation plays a role in the regulation of platelet secretion and aggregation.
LPA-induced platelet shape change is mediated by Rho-kinases/LIMK-kinases/cofilin, but LPA-induced secretion and aggregation are not.
LPA-induced shape change is regulated by Rho-kinases/LIMK-kinases and that secretion and aggregation are regulated by Ca(2+)/phosphatases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cofilin de-phosphorylation in platelets stimulated with LPA is independent of LIMK activation.

LIMK- and cofilin-mediated regulation of the actin cytoskeleton is a complex process that is regulated by a number of kinases and phosphatases and that the regulation of these kinases and phosphotases is also very complex.
cofilin de-phosphorylation is a very early event in LPA-stimulation of platelets, and it is independent of LIMK activation.
